# orders-api configuration module (Azure Container Apps)

Generated by `docuconf terraform -target containerapps` from the `orders-api` contract. It takes one argument per input, checks it against the contract, and renders a container app's secrets, its container's `env`, and the secret volume and mounts of its file inputs. See [spec/IAC.md](https://github.com/Docuconf/docuconf-go/blob/main/spec/IAC.md).

| Input | Type | Required | Set with | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ALLOWED_ORIGINS` | list |  | `value`, `injected` | Origins allowed to call the API from a browser |
| `DATABASE_URL` | url, secret | yes | `secret`, `injected` | Postgres connection string for the orders database |
| `LOG_LEVEL` | enum |  | `value`, `injected` | Minimum log level emitted |
| `PORT` | int |  | `value`, `injected` | HTTP listen port |
| `REQUEST_TIMEOUT` | duration |  | `value`, `injected` | Time limit for handling one request |
| `WEBHOOK_KEYS` | keySet, secret |  | `secret`, `injected` | Keys that verify the signature on incoming payment webhooks |
| `WORKER_COUNT` | int |  | `value`, `injected` | Number of background workers processing orders |
| `discounts` | config file at `/etc/orders/discounts/discounts.yaml` |  | `secret`, `injected` | Discount codes accepted at checkout |

A secret is a Key Vault secret ID, versioned or not, and the `identity` that reads it: `System` (the default) for the app's system-assigned identity, or a user-assigned identity's resource ID. That identity must be able to read the secret (the Key Vault Secrets User role). The module names the app secret it adds for each input (`dc-…`); add `containerapp_secrets` to the app's own secrets. A file input is one secret in a Secret volume, mounted at its path, and Container Apps sets its permissions; tls inputs, which are directories, and overlays, which need a ConfigMap, are not part of this module.

## Usage

```hcl
module "orders_api_config" {
  source = "./modules/orders-api-config"
  DATABASE_URL = { secret = { key_vault_secret_id = azurerm_key_vault_secret.database_url.versionless_id } }
}

resource "azurerm_container_app" "app" {
  # …
  # The dynamic blocks are not in the plan's configuration, so this
  # reference is what binds the app to the module for docuconf lint.
  tags = { app = module.orders_api_config.contract.name }
  identity {
    type = "SystemAssigned"
  }
  dynamic "secret" {
    for_each = module.orders_api_config.containerapp_secrets
    content {
      name                = secret.value.name
      key_vault_secret_id = secret.value.key_vault_secret_id
      identity            = secret.value.identity
    }
  }
  template {
    container {
      image = var.image
      # …
      dynamic "env" {
        for_each = module.orders_api_config.containerapp_env
        content {
          name        = env.value.name
          value       = env.value.value
          secret_name = env.value.secret_name
        }
      }
      dynamic "volume_mounts" {
        for_each = module.orders_api_config.containerapp_volume_mounts
        content {
          name     = volume_mounts.value.name
          path     = volume_mounts.value.path
          sub_path = volume_mounts.value.sub_path
        }
      }
    }
    dynamic "volume" {
      for_each = module.orders_api_config.containerapp_volumes
      content {
        name         = volume.value.name
        storage_type = volume.value.storage_type
      }
    }
  }
}
```

A system-assigned identity is created with the app, so it cannot be granted the secrets before the app's first revision reads them; with Key Vault references, a user-assigned identity granted in advance avoids a failed first deploy.
